parts.name: Hotkey Listener
parts.responsibility: Detects the global hotkey to start/stop dictation.

parts.name: Text Injector
parts.responsibility: Types or pastes the final text into the focused application. Uses CGEvent (macOS) or xdotool/ydotool (Linux). Falls back to clipboard+paste.

parts.name: Configuration
parts.responsibility: Stores user settings: hotkey binding, model paths, LLM model name, audio device.

parts.name: Transcriber
parts.responsibility: Runs one recording end to end. Its audio-consumer thread pulls the device's samples from AudioDevice's ring buffer, runs AudioProcessor (mono, 16 kHz), reports the audio level, and writes the audio into a per-recording ring buffer for the STT thread. On stop it joins that thread, flushes STT and runs the LLM on the raw transcript.

operations.signature: fn new(config: &Config, on_level: Arc<dyn Fn(f32) + Send + Sync>) -> Result<Self, TranscriberError>

operations.name: Audio level
post: level is the mic loudness in 0..=1, about 20 times a second while recording

state.name: STT audio buffer
invariants: one ring buffer per recording, holding 10 s of 16 kHz audio
the STT thread drains it every 10 ms while recording, and fully on Flush

failures.what: The device's format can't be processed (AudioProcessor::new fails)

recovery.detail: Stop capture, clear is_transcribing and log the format

failures.what: The STT thread falls more than 10 s behind, so the STT audio buffer is full
failures.detectedBy: send_audio reports samples that did not fit

recovery.detail: Drop those samples and log how many when the recording stops

parts.name: AudioDevice
parts.responsibility: Opens the capture device. Its real-time callback only scales each sample to f32 in -1..=1 and pushes the device's native interleaved samples into a ring buffer; nothing else runs there. Reports the native format (sample rate, channels).

failures.what: We cannot acquire audio device at init

parts.name: ParakeetSTT
parts.responsibility: Implements STT on the stt-warm thread. Silero VAD cuts the 16 kHz audio at pauses of at least 1 s (segments at most 20 s, with 0.3 s of pre-roll), and Parakeet transcribes each segment for the subscriber. Must be spawned in a thread.

parts.name: STT
parts.responsibility: Speech to text over 16 kHz mono f32 audio, delivered in segments to one subscriber.

operations.signature: fn subscribe(&mut self, on_transcribe: Box<dyn Fn(String) + Send>)

operations.name: Flush
post: all pushed audio has been transcribed and delivered

parts.name: LLM PostProcessor
parts.responsibility: The LLM PostProcessor incorporates the model running on mistral-rs. We'll prompt and wait for the response.

parts.name: AudioProcessor
parts.responsibility: Turns the device's interleaved samples into mono at the STT rate (16 kHz): averages the channels and resamples with rubato. All buffers are allocated in new, so process never allocates. Runs on Transcriber's audio-consumer thread, never in the real-time callback.

operations.name: New
operations.signature: fn new(format: InputFormat, output_rate: u32, max_block: usize) -> Option<Self>

operations.name: Process
pre: interleaved holds at most max_block samples
post: returns the resampled audio that became ready; a frame may span calls

operations.name: Finish
post: returns the audio still held by the resampler and resets for the next recording

state.name: Pending
invariants: capacity is set in new and never grows

guarantees.notes: Audio reaches the STT thread through the per-recording ring buffer, and that thread calls push_audio. Flush is sent only after the audio-consumer thread has been joined, so all audio is drained first.

tests.name: Happy path: speak and inject

given.notes: App is running, models loaded, user focused a text field

steps.does: User presses Ctrl+Alt+Space and says "Send the report to Anna"
Event Handler calls start_transcribing; the STT thread receives a new 10 s ring buffer
The audio-consumer thread opens the mic; the callback only scales 48 kHz mono samples into AudioDevice's ring buffer
Each 480-sample block becomes 160 samples at 16 kHz, written to the STT ring buffer; on_level reports about 0.7 while the user speaks
Every 10 ms the STT thread drains the ring buffer into push_audio; VAD holds the speech as one open segment
Event Handler calls stop_transcribing; is_transcribing clears and Transcriber joins the audio-consumer thread
Before exiting, the audio-consumer thread writes the resampler's tail into the STT ring buffer
Transcriber sends Flush; the STT thread drains what is left in the ring buffer, then flushes
VAD closes the open segment and Parakeet transcribes it
The STT subscriber appends "Send the report to Anna." to the raw transcript
clean_transcript keeps every word and fixes punctuation
Event Handler types "Send the report to Anna." into the focused text field

then: Clean text appears in the focused application

questions.text: What does WhisperFlow do? (a few sentences — what the user does, what happens, what comes out)
questions.why: I need the core flow to know what we're replicating locally.
options: It's a public project I can link

answer.text: It's a public project I can link

questions.text: When you say "running all locally" — what does that mean to you?
questions.why: It could mean no cloud API calls, self-hosted on your own server, or fully offline on one machine.

questions.text: What's the link? (GitHub repo, website, etc.)
questions.why: I'll read it to understand the flow before we design the local version.

questions.text: Which local STT engine are you thinking?
questions.why: Determines latency, accuracy, and resource requirements.

questions.text: For the LLM post-processing step, what do you have in mind?
questions.why: A small local model can clean text but quality varies; this affects which model and how much cleanup to expect.

questions.text: What platform is this for?
questions.why: Hotkey handling and text injection are very different on macOS vs Linux vs cross-platform.

questions.text: What language/runtime are you thinking for the app itself?
questions.why: Affects which libraries are available for hotkey, audio, and text injection.

questions.text: How should Parakeet integrate with the Rust app?
questions.why: Parakeet is from NVIDIA NeMo (Python). Options: sherpa-onnx (Rust bindings, ONNX runtime), or a Python sidecar process.

questions.text: How should the LLM connect?
questions.why: Ollama exposes a local HTTP API; llama.cpp has Rust FFI bindings.

answer.text: we can use mistral-rs, it's a small model and only needs to do inference

questions.text: Should transcription stream partial results while speaking, or wait until you stop?
questions.why: Streaming gives live feedback but adds complexity; batch is simpler and Parakeet is fast.

answer.text: partial text while speaking, call LLM only with final text

questions.text: How should the user see feedback (recording, processing, done)?
questions.why: Affects which UI libraries we need and how complex the overlay is.
options: System tray icon with color change

questions.text: Any preference for the global hotkey library?
questions.why: Rust options: device-query (simple), rdev (low-level), or tauri-plugin-global-shortcut (if using Tauri for overlay).

questions.text: For text injection, which approach do you prefer?
questions.why: Simulated keystrokes are universal but slow for long text; clipboard+paste is fast but clobbers the clipboard; CGEvent/xdotool is fast but platform-specific.
options: Platform-native (CGEvent on macOS, xdotool on Linux)
Clipboard + paste as default, keystrokes as fallback

answer.text: Platform-native (CGEvent on macOS, xdotool on Linux)

questions.text: Should the app auto-start on login?
questions.why: Affects whether we need a launch agent (macOS) or systemd user service (Linux).

questions.text: Which failure scenarios should we design recovery for first?
questions.why: Every failure needs a strategy; these are the most likely ones for a local dictation app.
options: STT model fails to load or crashes
LLM produces garbage or times out
Text injection fails (no accessibility permission on macOS)

questions.text: If text injection fails (e.g. accessibility permission denied), what should happen?
questions.why: The user spoke something — losing it is the worst outcome.
options: Copy to clipboard + notify user to paste manually
Show text in overlay for manual copy

questions.text: What goes in this module?
questions.why: I see you added it — want me to help fill it in, or are you sketching something?

questions.text: Does Transcriber replace both the `capture` and `stt` parts, or does it wrap them?
questions.why: If Transcriber owns audio + STT internally, the top-level capture and stt parts become implementation details inside it.
options: Transcriber replaces capture + stt (they become internal)
Transcriber wraps them (they stay as separate parts it calls)
Transcriber is just the STT part renamed

questions.text: Should I remove the `stt` part and route through Transcriber, or does Transcriber call `stt` internally (stt stays as a separate part)?
questions.why: Right now both exist — Transcriber and stt. One should own the STT logic.
options: Remove stt — Transcriber owns it internally
Keep stt — Transcriber calls it (stt is the sherpa-onnx wrapper)

answer.text: Remove stt — Transcriber owns it internally

questions.text: Who calls `push_audio` on the STT trait?
questions.why: Determines whether Transcriber is a middleman or AudioDevice talks to STT directly.
options: Transcriber pulls from HeapCons, pushes to STT
AudioDevice pushes directly to STT (holds a trait object)

answer.text: Transcriber pulls from HeapCons, pushes to STT
